info.name: Auth Service · complete API
info.description:
# Auth Service · complete API

Runnable Postman collection for every HTTP route exposed by this repository: probes, JWKS, signup, verification, sessions, applications, users, grants, invitations, password resets, MFA (TOTP), audit and access-control checks.

## Before running

1. Start MongoDB and MailHog: `docker-compose up -d`.
2. Copy the environment: `cp .env.example .env` and set `MONGO_URI`.
3. Provision the owner: set `OWNER_EMAIL`/`OWNER_PASSWORD` in `.env` (startup is idempotent) or run `OWNER_EMAIL=... OWNER_PASSWORD=... pnpm bootstrap:owner`.
4. Start the service: `pnpm dev`.
5. Import this collection and `auth-service.local.postman_environment.json`, select the environment and run it top to bottom.

## Access levels

- **Public** — no token.
- **Authenticated** — any valid access token; `{{accessToken}}` is the owner token and `{{appAccessToken}}` the application-scoped one.
- **Owner** — global owner only (`/users`, `/applications`, `/audit-events`, reset links).
- **App admin** — the owner or a grant with role `admin` on the application in the path.

## Tokens and variables

The test scripts save every identifier the next request needs: `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `appAccessToken`, `applicationId`, `userId`, `holderId`, `invitationToken`, `resetToken`, `sessionId`, `mfaSecret`, `mfaToken`, `recoveryCode`, `jwt` kid, and so on. Refresh requests rotate the stored refresh token automatically.

`03 · Applications → Create application` regenerates a unique slug, audience and demo emails on every execution, so the collection can be replayed without duplicate-key errors. Applications have no delete endpoint yet: each run leaves one behind.

## Local notes

- Verification and reset codes are read from MailHog (`http://localhost:8025`) by the two `MailHog · ...` requests. The extraction is best effort; copy the code into `{{verificationCode}}`/`{{resetCode}}` if it fails.
- MFA codes are computed in the request pre-scripts with `crypto-js` from `{{mfaSecret}}`; no authenticator app is required.
- The dev `.env.example` allows 15 logins, 15 signups, 10 password resets and 20 refreshes per 5 seconds, plus a global 100 requests / 15 minutes per IP. A full run stays below those limits; running the collection repeatedly may hit the global one.
- `14 · Cleanup` is destructive (revokes sessions, logs out, deletes the demo users). Skip it to keep the fixtures.

## Headers

Authenticated requests use `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. JSON bodies send `Content-Type: application/json`.

item.name: 00 · Probes and keys
item.description: Public endpoints: liveness, readiness and the JWKS. No token needed.

request.description:
`GET /health` — **Public**. Liveness probe; it never touches MongoDB.

Expected: `200 { "status": "ok" }`.

`GET /ready` — **Public**. Readiness probe.

Expected: `200 { "status": "ready" }`, or `503 { "status": "not ready" }` when MongoDB is not connected.

exec: pm.test('returns at least one public key', () => {

request.description:
`GET /.well-known/jwks.json` — **Public**. RS256 public keys, cacheable for 5 minutes.

Expected: `200 { "keys": [ { "kid": "...", "kty": "RSA", ... } ] }`. Only public material is published.

item.name: 01 · Signup and email verification
item.description: Self-service account creation. The holder is temporary and the emailed code is single-use.

request.description:
`POST /auth/signup` — **Public**, rate-limited.

Creates a holder (not a user yet) and mails a 6-character code. The response never includes the password.

Expected: `201 { "_id", "email", "expiresAt", "createdAt", "updatedAt" }`. `_id` is the `holderId` needed to verify.

Each execution generates a fresh `signupEmail` so the request can be replayed without a duplicate-email error.

exec: pm.expect(mailhogMessage, 'No matching email: is MailHog running? Did the service send it?')
pm.expect(mailhogMatch, 'Copy the 6-character code from MailHog into the collection variable manually').to.not.be.null;

request.description:
Reads MailHog (not the auth service) and stores the verification code in `{{verificationCode}}`.

MailHog web UI: <http://localhost:8025>. If the extraction fails, copy the code manually into the collection variable.

`POST /auth/verify?holderId=...` — **Public**.

Consumes the emailed code, creates the verified user and deletes the holder.

Expected: `204` with no body. Replaying it returns `400 INVALID_CODE`.

item.name: 02 · Owner session
item.description: The owner logs in without an application and receives a global token (no `aud`). This token authorises the catalogue, users, links and audit.

exec: pm.expect(body.mfaRequired, 'The owner has MFA enabled: complete the MFA folder or disable it first').to.be.undefined;
pm.test('issues an access and a refresh token', () => {

request.description:
`POST /auth/login` — **Public**, rate-limited.

Without `application` only the global owner can log in. Provision it with `OWNER_EMAIL`/`OWNER_PASSWORD` or `pnpm bootstrap:owner`.

Expected: `200 { "accessToken", "refreshToken" }`. If the owner has MFA enabled this request returns an MFA challenge instead: finish the MFA folder or disable MFA first.

`GET /auth/me` — **Authenticated**. Returns the identity behind the presented token.

Expected: `200 { "id", "email", "application": null, "role": "owner", "expiresAt" }`.

`POST /auth/introspect` — **Authenticated**. The caller only sees its own tokens, in the same application.

Expected: `200 { "active": true, "id", "application": null, "role": "owner", "expiresAt" }`.

exec: pm.test('issues an access and a refresh token', () => {

request.description:
`POST /auth/refresh` — **Public**, rate-limited. Rotates the refresh token: the previous one is revoked.

Expected: `200 { "accessToken", "refreshToken" }` with a different refresh token.

`GET /auth/sessions` — **Authenticated**. Active device sessions, newest activity first.

Expected: `200 [ { "id", "device", "application", "ipAddress", "createdAt", "lastActivityAt", "expiresAt" } ]`.

`{{sessionId}}` is overwritten with the most recent session (the one from the last login).

item.name: 03 · Applications
item.description: Owner-only catalogue. Each execution of **Create application** generates a fresh slug, audience and demo emails so the run is replayable.

request.description:
`POST /applications` — **Owner**.

Expected: `201 { "_id", "name", "slug", "audience", "active": true, ... }`.

The pre-request script regenerates `runId`, the slug, the audience and the demo emails, and clears the identifiers of the previous run.
`GET /applications` — **Owner**. Expected: `200 [ ... ]`.
`GET /applications/:id` — **Owner**. Expected: `200` with the application, or `404 NOT_FOUND`.

item.name: 04 · Users
item.description: Owner-only user administration. `POST /users` creates a verified user directly, without the email round-trip.

request.description:
`POST /users` — **Owner**.

Expected: `201 { "_id", "email", "role": "user", "verified": true, ... }`. The password is never serialised.

The created user is the account used later for grants, application login and MFA.

`GET /users` — **Owner**. Expected: `200 [ ... ]`.

The script also locates the account created by the signup folder and stores `{{signupUserId}}` for cleanup.
`GET /users/:id` — **Owner**. Expected: `200` with the user, or `404 NOT_FOUND`.

exec: pm.test('trims and stores the chat id', () => {

request.description:
`PATCH /users/:id` — **Owner**. Accepts profile fields; `role` is ignored on purpose.

Expected: `200` with the updated user and the trimmed `telegramChatId`.

`PATCH /users/:id` — **Owner**. `null` clears the optional chat id.

Expected: `200` and no `telegramChatId` in the response.

item.name: 05 · Grants
item.description: Per-application permissions: `viewer`, `editor` and `admin`. The owner can manage every application; an app admin only its own.

request.description:
`PUT /applications/:applicationId/grants` — **App admin**. Idempotent upsert.

Expected: `200 { "_id", "userId", "applicationId", "role": "editor", ... }`.

`PUT /applications/:applicationId/grants` — **App admin**. Repeating the call with another role updates it, so the user can also invite guests later.

Expected: `200` with `"role": "admin"`.
`GET /applications/:applicationId/grants` — **App admin**. Expected: `200 [ ... ]`.
`GET /applications/:applicationId/grants/:userId` — **App admin**. Expected: `200` with the grant, or `404 NOT_FOUND`.

`DELETE /applications/:applicationId/grants/:userId` — **App admin**. Revoking removes the permission; the user keeps the account.

Expected: `204`. The next request restores the grant so the application login still works.

`PUT /applications/:applicationId/grants` — **App admin**. Re-assigns the role used by the rest of the run.

Expected: `200` with `"role": "admin"`.

item.name: 06 · Application login
item.description: The user exchanges credentials plus an application slug or audience for a scoped token. Only users with an active grant can log in.

exec: pm.test('issues an access and a refresh token', () => {

request.description:
`POST /auth/login` — **Public**, rate-limited.

Expected: `200 { "accessToken", "refreshToken" }`. The token carries the application `aud` and the grant role.

The tokens are stored in `{{appAccessToken}}` and `{{appRefreshToken}}`, keeping the owner tokens intact.

`GET /auth/me` — **Authenticated**. With an application token it reports the audience and the grant role.

Expected: `200 { "id", "email", "application": "<audience>", "role": "admin", "expiresAt" }`.

exec: pm.test('issues an access and a refresh token', () => {

request.description:
`POST /auth/refresh` — **Public**, rate-limited. The grant is re-checked on every rotation.

Expected: `200` with a new pair, still scoped to the same application.
`POST /auth/introspect` — **Authenticated**. Expected: `200 { "active": true, "application": "<audience>", "role": "admin", ... }`.

item.name: 07 · Invitations
item.description: Single-use links that let a guest set a password and receive a grant. The link is hashed at rest and can be delivered through Telegram.

exec: console.warn('Could not parse the invitation link: ' + error.message);

request.description:
`POST /applications/:applicationId/invitations` — **App admin**.

Expected: `201 { "link", "expiresAt", "email", "applicationId", "role", "notification": { "delivered", "recipient" } }`.

The script stores the `token` query parameter in `{{invitationToken}}`. Delivery is best effort: `notification.delivered: false` still returns a copyable link.

`POST /auth/invitations/accept` — **Public**.

Sets the password, creates a verified user and grants the invited role. The link is consumed atomically.

Expected: `204`. Repeating it returns `400 INVALID_LINK`.

`POST /auth/login` — **Public**, rate-limited.

Expected: `200` with a token scoped to the application and the invited `editor` role.
`GET /auth/me` — **Authenticated**. Expected: `200` with `"role": "editor"` and the application audience.

item.name: 08 · Password reset links
item.description: Owner-generated single-use links, useful when email delivery is not configured. The alternative email-code flow is in the next folder.

exec: console.warn('Could not parse the reset link: ' + error.message);

request.description:
`POST /auth/password-reset-links` — **Owner**.

Expected: `201 { "link", "expiresAt", "userId", "notification" }`. The script stores the token in `{{resetToken}}`.

`POST /auth/password-reset-links/accept` — **Public**.

Consumes the link and rotates the password. Every session of the user is revoked.

Expected: `204`. The script updates `{{targetUserPassword}}` to the new value.

exec: pm.test('issues an access and a refresh token', () => {

request.description: `POST /auth/login` — **Public**, rate-limited. Confirms the reset and refreshes the application tokens used by the MFA folder.

item.name: 09 · Forgot password · email code
item.description: The public, reveal-nothing alternative: the service mails a code only when the account exists.

request.description:
`POST /auth/forgot-password` — **Public**, rate-limited.

Expected: `204` whether or not the email exists (no account enumeration).

exec: pm.expect(mailhogMessage, 'No matching email: is MailHog running? Did the service send it?')
pm.expect(mailhogMatch, 'Copy the 6-character code from MailHog into the collection variable manually').to.not.be.null;

request.description: Reads MailHog and stores the reset code in `{{resetCode}}`. Best effort: copy it manually if the extraction fails.

item.name: Reset the password with the code

request.description:
`POST /auth/reset-password` — **Public**. Needs `userId` + the emailed code.

Expected: `204`. Every session of the user is revoked.

exec: pm.test('issues an access and a refresh token', () => {

request.description: `POST /auth/login` — **Public**, rate-limited. Confirms the code-based reset and refreshes the application tokens.

item.name: 10 · Device sessions
item.description: Every login creates an independent session. This folder revokes a second session without touching the token used by the rest of the collection.

exec: pm.expect(body.accessToken, 'The owner has MFA enabled: disable it before running this folder').to.be.a('string').and.not.empty;

request.description:
`POST /auth/login` — **Public**, rate-limited. Creates a second owner session.

The tokens go to `{{sessionProbeAccessToken}}` so the main owner token stays valid.

item.name: List sessions after the second login

exec: pm.test('has more than one active session', () => {

request.description:
`GET /auth/sessions` — **Authenticated**. Sessions are ordered by `lastActivityAt`, so the first one is the probe session just created.

Expected: `200` with at least two sessions; `{{sessionId}}` points at the newest one.

`DELETE /auth/sessions/:sessionId` — **Authenticated**.

Expected: `204`. Repeating it is a no-op. The session’s refresh token stops working; the access token keeps working until it expires.

item.name: 11 · MFA · TOTP
item.description: Enrollment, activation, challenge login and disable. The pre-request scripts compute the current TOTP from `{{mfaSecret}}` with crypto-js, so no manual code is needed.

exec: pm.test('returns a base32 secret and an otpauth URL', () => {

request.description:
`POST /auth/mfa/enroll` — **Authenticated**, rate-limited. Requires the current password.

Expected: `200 { "secret", "otpauthUrl" }`. The secret is stored in `{{mfaSecret}}`; add the `otpauthUrl` to any authenticator if you want to follow along manually.

`POST /auth/mfa/activate` — **Authenticated**. Confirms the first TOTP code.

Expected: `200 { "recoveryCodes": [ ... 10 codes ... ] }`. The first recovery code is stored in `{{recoveryCode}}`; codes are shown only once.

exec: pm.test('returns an MFA challenge instead of tokens', () => {

request.description:
`POST /auth/login` — **Public**, rate-limited. With MFA enabled the response has no tokens.

Expected: `200 { "mfaRequired": true, "challengeToken", "expiresIn": 300 }`. The challenge is stored in `{{mfaToken}}`.

exec: pm.test('issues an access and a refresh token', () => {

request.description:
`POST /auth/mfa/verify` — **Public**, rate-limited. Exchanges the challenge plus a TOTP or recovery code for tokens.

Expected: `200 { "accessToken", "refreshToken" }`.

`POST /auth/mfa/disable` — **Authenticated**, rate-limited. Needs the password and a TOTP or recovery code.

Expected: `204`. You can replace `{{mfaCode}}` with `{{recoveryCode}}` to consume a recovery code instead.

exec: pm.test('issues an access and a refresh token', () => {

request.description: `POST /auth/login` — **Public**, rate-limited. Confirms the account returns to password-only login.

item.name: 12 · Audit log
item.description: Owner-only, read-only view of the security events recorded by the service. Only identifiers and request metadata are stored.

request.description:
`GET /audit-events` — **Owner**.

Expected: `200 [ { "_id", "event", "result", "userId", "email", "createdAt", ... } ]`. `{{auditEvent}}` keeps the newest event name for the filtered request.

`GET /audit-events?event=...` — **Owner**. Accepted events: `login.succeeded`, `login.failed`, `login.locked`, `token.refreshed`, `session.logged_out`, `session.revoked`, `session.revoked_all`, `grant.assigned`, `grant.revoked`.

item.name: Filter by user and date range

request.description: `GET /audit-events?userId=...&from=...&to=...` — **Owner**. A date-only `to` includes the whole day. The pre-request script uses yesterday and today.

item.name: 13 · Access-control checks
item.description: Intentional denials. Each one asserts the status the service must return, so a green run proves the authentication middleware still rejects anonymous and application-scoped tokens.

request.description:
`GET /applications` — **Owner**. Without `Authorization: Bearer` the request is rejected by the authentication middleware.

Expected: `401 { "message": "Invalid or missing authorization header", "code": "INVALID_CREDENTIALS" }`.

item.name: Application token on an owner route · 401

request.description:
`GET /users` — **Owner**. The authentication middleware rejects a scoped token before the role guard runs: an application token carries `aud`, and owner routes only accept the unscoped owner token.

Expected: `401 { "message": "Invalid token payload", "code": "INVALID_CREDENTIALS" }`. A `403` is not reachable here: `/auth/login` only issues unscoped tokens to the owner.

item.name: Introspect a foreign token · active false

exec: pm.test('does not reveal another user\'s token', () => {

request.description:
`POST /auth/introspect` — **Authenticated**. A caller can only introspect its own tokens.

Expected: `200 { "active": false }` and no extra data about the guest token.

item.name: 14 · Cleanup · optional
item.description: Destructive: revokes sessions, logs out and deletes the demo users. Run it last, or skip it if you want to keep the fixtures. Applications have no delete endpoint yet, so each run leaves one behind.

request.description:
`DELETE /auth/sessions` — **Authenticated**. Revokes every refresh token of the caller; the current access token stays valid until it expires.

Expected: `204`.

`POST /auth/logout` — **Authenticated**. Blacklists the current access token and revokes the sessions of the token’s application.

Expected: `204`. No body is required (the route is excluded from the required-body middleware).

`DELETE /users/:id` — **Owner**. Cascades the guest grant.

Expected: `204`.

`DELETE /users/:id` — **Owner**. Cascades the application grant.

Expected: `204`.

`DELETE /users/:id` — **Owner**. Removes the account created by the signup folder.

Expected: `204`. Needs the full run: `{{signupUserId}}` is filled by **List users**.

`POST /auth/logout` — **Authenticated**. Unscoped owner tokens revoke every owner session.

Expected: `204`. After this request, log in again to keep exploring.
